sections.title: Roll to cast
sections.md:
There are **no spell slots**. Morten can cast any spell he has prepared, as often as he likes, but every cast needs a **casting check**:

- **Roll:** d20 + INT mod + proficiency bonus (his spell attack bonus) vs **DC 10 + the spell's level**. Cantrips are DC 10.
- **Success:** the spell works as written.
- **Failure:** the spell fizzles (the action is spent) and that spell is **lost until he finishes a Long Rest**: it can't be cast again, cantrips included.
- **Natural 20:** it works, and he doubles one numeric effect of his choice (damage dice, duration, number of targets, area), or for a spell attack it is a critical hit instead.
- **Natural 1:** it fails, the spell is lost, and he rolls 1d12 on the **mishap table** below.
- **Spell attacks** use one roll for both. The total must meet the DC to cast and beat the target's AC to hit. Total < DC: fizzle, lost. DC ≤ total < AC: cast but missed (Potent Cantrip still applies). Total ≥ AC: hit. With several attacks (*Scorching Ray*), the first attack roll is the casting check; the rest are plain attack rolls.
- **Save spells:** cast first, then targets save against his spell save DC as normal.
- **Casting at a higher level:** he may cast a spell as if from a higher-level slot, up to the highest slot level his Wizard level would give (level 2 at Wizard 3). The DC uses that higher level.
- **Rituals:** casting a Ritual spell as a Ritual (the +10 minutes) needs no check.
- **Mage Armor from Magic Initiate:** once per Long Rest he may cast it with no check. Otherwise it follows the normal roll.
- **Arcane Recovery:** once per Long Rest, when he finishes a Short Rest, he regains lost spells whose levels add up to no more than half his Wizard level (round up). A cantrip counts as level 1.
- **Heroic Inspiration** (Human) may reroll a casting check. With Advantage or Disadvantage, it rerolls one of the two dice.
- **The casting check is an ability check**, so anything that affects ability checks affects it (Poisoned gives Disadvantage). Advantage on a spell attack (a Restrained or Unconscious target) also helps that same roll, since the attack roll is the casting check.
- **Magic items and scrolls** cast their spells with no casting check.
- Concentration works as written.

**Wizard mishap table (1d12)**

| d12 | Mishap |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Backlash.** Morten takes 2d6 force damage. |
| 2 | **Wild target.** The spell goes off anyway, but at a random creature in range (Morten included). Roll the target. |
| 3 | **Burnout.** Every other prepared spell of the same level (or every cantrip) is also lost until Long Rest. |
| 4 | **Snuffed.** All light within 9 m goes out: torches, lamps, *Light* ends. Relighting a torch takes an action and a tinderbox. |
| 5 | **Thunderclap.** A crack heard 90 m away. The GM rolls a wandering monster check right away, with a 1–3 on d6 meaning an encounter. |
| 6 | **Drained.** 1 level of Exhaustion. |
| 7 | **Glow.** He sheds bright violet light in 3 m for 1 minute, can't Hide, and attack rolls against him have Advantage until the end of his next turn. |
| 8 | **Slipped grip.** He drops everything he's holding, focus included. |
| 9 | **Tongue-tied.** He can't cast spells with a Verbal component until the end of his next turn. |
| 10 | **Unravel.** Every spell he is maintaining (concentration, Mage Armor, *Light*) ends. |
| 11 | **Spell worm.** One random other prepared spell is lost until Long Rest. |
| 12 | **Fizzle.** Nothing else happens. |

sections.title: Death and the respawn
sections.md:
- Dying works as written: at 0 HP he makes Death Saving Throws, and he dies on three failures, on massive damage, or from an effect that kills outright (a Shadow taking his Strength to 0).
- When he dies, he **revives at the dungeon's entrance camp**, at full HP, with all spells restored and all conditions and Exhaustion removed. It counts as a Long Rest; 8 hours pass.
- He **loses all coins and gems he was carrying**. He keeps everything else: gear, magic items, spellbook, XP. Gold stored nowhere is safe; there is no bank.
- The dungeon stays as he left it: dead monsters stay dead, looted rooms stay looted, but living monsters have 8 hours to move, regroup and reset their traps.
- Track deaths in the GM's notes (Deaths: N).
- The camp has a trader who sells anything in the SRD's equipment lists at listed price, plus Potions of Healing (50 GP), and buys gear at half price, gems at full value. That's where gold matters.

sections.title: This campaign's rules
sections.md:
Public: Morten may know all of this. These add to the game's rules and the GM's notes (Realms v3), and win where they differ.

- **The world** comes from the engine. Nothing in the world is hidden from the tower but the dungeon floors.
- **Morten** starts fresh: the pre-built Wizard 3 (Evoker), 900 XP, his starting gear and 47 GP 7 SP 5 CP. He starts in his tower (B5) on Month 1 · Day 1 at 08:00, rested. The tower starts as **Hermit** (Renown 0), Hold 3 of 3, 100 GP, no sites, no goal, holding only its warded hex.
- **Dungeon floors (Delve).** Each hex holds the floor of its level. A floor works like the demo dungeon's: a chain of rooms (entrance → room 1 → room 2 → … → the end), one monster type per room, each room with a size and one terrain feature. He can't skip a room without getting through it (fighting, sneaking or teleporting past all count; bypassed monsters still give their XP).
  - **No camps and no stairs between floors.** The entrance is in the hex; leaving the floor ends the Delve.
  - **No wandering monsters** inside a floor.
  - **Loot:** each room's monsters drop coins worth a tenth of their XP, once.
  - Dead monsters stay dead. Survivors are back at full HP in their room after any 8 hours he spends away.
- **Missions:** one a month, in the hex he is in: **Strike** a site, **Rob** a realm's works, **Aid** a realm's goal, **Contact** a realm (a Persuasion check), or **Delve**.
- **Mission fights** (Strike, Rob, Aid) are built by the engine (a Strike or Rob on that site) or the engine (an Aid), from the site's fight list at its tier, at the tier's budget for his level (tier 1 Low, 2 Moderate, 3 High). Their coins are a tenth of their XP, as in a floor.
- **Death** sends him back to the tower, not to a camp: the month's mission fails, he loses the coins and gems he carried, the purse actions stand.
- **The purse.** Coins he leaves in the tower are safe from death but are not the tower's treasury until he deposits them at the world's turn.
- **Downtime.** After the month's mission the rest of the month passes: Morten finishes a Long Rest where he is (full HP, spells, Heroic Inspiration and the free Mage Armor back) and lives off his own land. Rations count only on travel and mission days.

sections.title: Sites: what Morten can strike
sections.md:
A site sits in one hex and belongs to one realm (or the tower). It doesn't move, has no HP, never attacks and is never destroyed: a Strike on it moves clocks, nothing more. It exists to be a fight and to carry a modifier. When a hex changes holder its garrison, works and walls go with it; a seat is the ruler's and moves with the ruler instead.

| Site | Where | Fight (SRD, by tier) | Modifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Seat** | the ruler's hex | the court: Noble, Spy, Tough, Guard, Knight, Guard Captain, at the realm's tier **+1** (max 3) | — |
| **Garrison** | one hex | tier 1 Guard, Scout, Guard Captain · tier 2 Knight, Warrior Veteran, Warhorse · tier 3 Berserker, Warrior Veteran, Gladiator, Ogre, at the realm's tier | **−1** to any goal roll aimed at this hex |
| **Works** | one hex | Farms: Guard, Mastiff, Scout · Mine (hills or mountains): Tough, Guard, Tough Boss · Caravans (plains or savanna): Guard, Scout, Warrior Veteran, Mastiff, at the realm's tier **−1** (min 1) | the holder's **income +50 GP a month**; what Rob takes from |
| **Walls** | a hex a goal or the purse fortified (one per hex) | Animated Armor, Guard, Gargoyle, at the realm's tier | **−1** to goal rolls aimed at this hex; a *take* goal against a walled hex has a 6-mark clock (the tower's, +2) |
| **Beasts** | any hex, for Aid fights (section 9) | the hex's people's beasts: Humans Mastiff, Warhorse, Scout · Elves Giant Owl, Giant Eagle, Giant Elk · Orcs Worg, Dire Wolf, Giant Boar · Gnomes Giant Badger, Giant Goat, Brown Bear · Tieflings Imp, Hell Hound · Goblinkind Giant Hyena, Worg, Gnoll Warrior · the tower folk Mastiff, Giant Owl, Brown Bear | — |

Works are named by the biome of the hex they are built in (Mine in hills or mountains, Caravans in plains or savanna, Farms elsewhere) and keep the name when the hex changes hands. Sites have ids s1, s2, … in the order they were built, and show prints them. The tower's own sites are never fought: no realm attacks a site, and Morten doesn't strike his own (show lists them at tier 1, which never matters).

**Mission fights are D&D fights** built from a site's list by encounter: **tier 1 a Low encounter for Morten's level, tier 2 Moderate, tier 3 High**, at most 4 monsters of at most two kinds, coins a tenth of their XP. The hex level scales only wandering monsters and the dungeon floor.

Sites are **all open**: the map shows every site, every goal, every clock and every treasury. show prints all of it; there is no the engine.

sections.title: Goals and clocks
sections.md:
A goal is one line with a kind, a target and a clock. The clock's size is the goal's weight; marks fill it; a full clock fires the goal's effect at the world's turn. Marks never go above the size, never below 0.

### The roll

Once a month, each realm rolls **d6** for its goal, plus modifiers:

| Modifier | When |
|---|---|
| +1 / −1 | the goal has a target realm and this realm's Force is higher / lower (never against the tower: it has no Force) |
| −1 | the goal is aimed at a hex with a garrison; −1 more for walls (the tower's sites too; *break the tower* is aimed at the tower hex) |
| +1 | the tower gave this realm 200 GP or more this month (Give) |
| +1 / −1 | the tower backs / hinders it (the Warden's power, section 7) |

| Roll (after modifiers) | Marks |
|---|---|
| natural 1 | **setback:** −1 mark (min 0), whatever the modifiers |
| 2 or less | nothing |
| 3–5 | +1 |
| 6 or more | +2 |

A plain roll fills 0.67 marks a month, so a 4-clock takes about six months and a 2-clock three; with +1 it fills about 0.85 a month. Across six realms that is roughly one goal done somewhere every month, and each realm's line changes about every half year. **A won Strike takes 2 marks off** (section 9), a full third of a *take* clock: one fight is visible on the map.

### The catalogue

Every goal the script can hand out, resolve and explain. "Price" is paid from the realm's treasury when the clock fills; a goal it can't pay **waits full** ("done, waits for 300 GP") and fires the month the treasury covers it, rolling no more (a Strike that knocks it below full sends it back to rolling). A goal whose **target is gone** is **dropped** at the world's turn and a new one picked at once: a *take* whose hex already changed hands; a *fortify* whose hex is lost or walled already; a *raise* at Force 5; a *press* or *break* whose target is at Force 1 already; a *raid the tower*, *break the tower* or *take* of a tower hex by a realm that is now an ally; a *court the tower* by an ally.

| Goal | Clock | Target | Price at the end | Effect when the clock is full |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **take HEX** from REALM (or the tower) | 4 (6 if walled) | the holder | — | the hex changes holder with its garrison, works and walls; a seat there moves to the loser's deepest hex left; the loser **weighs "take back"** first when it next picks a goal |
| **fortify HEX** | 3 | — | 300 GP | Walls at HEX (one per hex) |
| **raise** | 3 | — | 200 × the new Force | Force +1 (max 5) |
| **raid REALM** (or the tower) | 2 | the richest neighbour | — | takes **100 × its own Force GP** from the target's treasury (at most what it holds; from the tower, at most half) |
| **press REALM** | 3 | the weakest neighbour | — | its own Force +1 (max 5), the target's Force −1 (min 1) |
| **squeeze** | 2 | — | — | treasury +100 GP per hex held; Contact in its hexes is DC +4 for the next 3 months |
| **break REALM** | 4 | a bad neighbour with lower Force | — | the target's Force −1 (min 1) |
| **break the tower** | 4 | the tower | — | the tower's **Hold −1** and half its treasury taken; at Hold 0, half the treasury and, instead of the box, the tower's deepest hex but the warded one changes holder with its sites (section 7); the realm's standing −1 (it is at war now) and it **rests** from the tower for 12 months |
| **court the tower** | 2 | the tower | — | its standing with the tower +1. This one can reach +2: the realm is an ally, and a running *ally REALM* goal of the tower's for it is done (section 10) |

### Who picks what

A realm with no goal picks one the moment it needs one at the world's turn, in this order, the first that applies. A goal picked because the old one fired rolls from the next month; one picked because the realm had none, or its goal's target was gone, rolls that same month. The d6s below are rolled and shown in the log; they come from a stream seeded by the world's seed and the month, so the same month rolls the same whatever Morten's orders were.

1. **Take back**, before anything, if the realm holds no land (section 3).
2. **Break the tower** if it is bad, not an ally, at standing 0 or less and not resting: at standing −1 or less, without a roll; at standing 0 when the tower is Warden or higher, on a d6 of 4+; at standing 0 as a **neighbour of the tower**, at any tier, on a d6 of **6**. A realm whose *break the tower* has fired **rests** from the tower for **12 months** and skips this rule until then, even at war.
3. **Take back** a hex of its own people it has lost, if its Force is at least the holder's. The deepest such hex. From the tower (which has no Force) at any Force, but never the warded hex and never by an ally.
4. **Court the tower** if it is good, at standing 0 or +1, and the tower is Lord or higher, on a d6 of 4+.
5. **Its tag's goal**, with the **rich** rule: a realm with **1,000 GP or more** whose tag would give it a goal with no price (*take*, *raid*, *press*, *squeeze*, *break*) picks **raise** instead (under Force 5; at Force 5, **fortify** its deepest unwalled hex), unless its last goal was a *raise* or a *fortify*. So a rich realm alternates its tag's goal with spending.

| Label | Tag | Shown as | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| bad | Conqueror | bad: takes land | **take** the deepest hex next to its own that is not a seat and not the warded hex, preferring one with **no garrison or walls**; a guarded one only when every border hex is guarded. An ally never a tower hex |
| bad | Raider | bad: robs its neighbours | **raid** the richest neighbour by treasury (the tower counts when it holds a hex next to the realm and is richest; a tie goes to a realm). An ally never the tower |
| bad | Slaver | bad: takes people for soldiers | **press** the weakest neighbour realm at Force 2 or more (ties: the poorer). A Slaver at Force 5 still presses: only the target's −1 lands |
| bad | Tyrant | bad: squeezes its own people | **squeeze**; after a squeeze, **fortify** its seat if unwalled, else **raise** (under Force 5); after a fortify, **raise**; otherwise squeeze again |
| good | Steward | good: keeps the peace | **fortify** its seat if unwalled; after a fortify, **raise** (under Force 5); else fortify its deepest unwalled hex; else raise; with everything walled at Force 5, rule 6 |
| good | Liberator | good: fights tyrants | **break** the weakest bad neighbour realm whose Force is lower than its own and at least 2; else as a Steward |

6. **Raise** if it has the price in hand and is under Force 5; else **fortify** its seat if unwalled; else **squeeze**.

An **ally** (+2) never aims a goal at the tower: not *break the tower*, not *raid the tower*, not a *take* of a tower hex (*take back* included); one it already holds is dropped. A goal not done after **12 months of rolling** (12 rolls, counted from its first roll) is dropped at clean-up, its marks lost, and a new one picked (6 months, the plan's number, kept dropping a *take* against a garrison and picking the same one again); a goal that waits full is not dropped.

sections.title: Standing, Hold, Renown and the ladder
sections.md:
### Standing

Each realm's attitude to the tower, one number:

| −2 enemy | −1 wary | 0 neutral | +1 friendly | +2 ally |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Change | Cause |
|---|---|
| −1 | Morten Strikes one of its sites (**−2** for its seat) or Robs it |
| −2 | the tower takes one of its hexes |
| +1 | a won Aid for it; a won Contact; the tower gives it 200 GP or more in a month (once a month). None of these lift it past +1: **ally is the tower's goal** (section 10) |
| +1 | its *court the tower* goal fires (this one can reach +2: an ally by its own deed, and the tower's *ally* goal for it, if running, is done) |
| = +2 | the tower's *ally* goal is done for it; a ruler the tower put on the throne |
| −1 | its *break the tower* goal fires (it is at war now, and rests from the tower for 12 months) |

**An ally** (+2) never aims a goal at the tower (section 5), and adds **+1 mark a month to the tower's goal** when that goal is *take* or *topple* (not *ally*; one ally counts, two at Power, section below; never the goal's own target). **An enemy** (−2) refuses Contact. Nothing drifts back on its own: standing moves only by deeds. Standing stays within −2 to +2.

### Hold

The tower's buffer: **3 boxes**. A *break the tower* goal that fires takes one box and half the treasury; at 0 boxes it takes half the treasury and, instead of the box, a hex of the tower's (its deepest, never the warded one) with the sites there; with no hex but the warded one, half the treasury only. **Mend** a box for 200 GP (a purse action). Hold is the only thing on the tower that can be hurt, and only by a goal the human watched fill for months.

### Renown and the ladder

**Renown** = hexes held beyond the tower hex + allies + 2 × rulers toppled. It is read off the map after every world's turn, never bought. The tier is the last row Renown reaches:

| Tier | Name | Renown | The power it brings |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Hermit | 0 | — |
| 1 | Lord of the hex | 2 | **Garrison** and **Walls** may be bought for the tower's hexes (purse actions, section 8). Wandering checks stop in a garrisoned tower hex |
| 2 | Warden of the marches | 5 | **Back** or **hinder** one realm's goal roll a month (+1 / −1) for 100 GP |
| 3 | A power in the land | 9 | Morten's Strike and Aid move **3 marks** instead of 2 (on the realm's goal and on the tower's); **two allies** count on the tower's goal |
| 4 | Master of the twenty hexes | 14 | May **set an ally's goal** from the catalogue each month (--set, section 12): the ally drops its goal and takes the set one at 0 marks, rolling for it that month. Reaching Master with **every realm an ally** (a toppled realm's new ruler is one, at +2) ends the campaign: the world is his |

Renown can fall (a hex lost; a toppled ruler is permanent). The tier falls with it; the report says so in one line.

**How the realms feel it:** from Warden on, bad rulers who aren't allies start weighing *break the tower* (section 5, rule 2), and good ones *court the tower* from Lord on. Rising makes enemies and friends at once, which is what the arc wants. A Hermit is not safe either: a bad neighbour of the tower at standing 0 weighs *break the tower* on a 6 whenever it picks a goal, so the tower at rest is attacked about twice in two years.

sections.title: Purse actions
sections.md:
Not goals and not limited to one: anything the treasury covers, declared with the month's orders and paid at the world's turn before the month's income, in this order: the tower's goal, the mission (a Rob's gold reaches the treasury first), deposit and withdraw, the purchases, Set, Give, back or hinder. A purse action the treasury can't cover at its turn, or the tier doesn't allow, is rejected with the orders.

| Action | Cost | Needs | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Garrison HEX** | 400 GP | Lord; a hex the tower holds; none there yet | a site: −1 to goal rolls aimed at that hex |
| **Walls HEX** | 600 GP | Lord; a garrison there; none there yet | −1 more; a *take* against it needs 6 marks |
| **Works HEX** | 300 GP | a hex the tower holds; none there yet | income +50 GP a month; a site a realm's Raid can target |
| **Mend** | 200 GP | Hold below 3 | Hold +1 |
| **Give REALM GP** | the GP | — | the gold is theirs. 200 GP or more in one month: +1 on its goal roll this month, standing +1 (once a month, to at most +1), and +1 on the tower's goal when that goal is *ally REALM*. While the tower's goal is *topple REALM*, a Give to REALM goes to its **dissident** instead: +1 on the topple clock (once a month) and nothing else |
| **Back / hinder REALM** | 100 GP | Warden | +1 / −1 on that realm's roll this month; one a month |
| **Set REALM GOAL** | — | Master; REALM an ally | REALM drops its goal and takes GOAL at 0 marks: *take HEX* (not its own, not the tower's), *fortify HEX* (an unwalled hex of its own), *raise*, *raid REALM*, *press REALM*, *squeeze* or *break REALM* |

**Deposit and withdraw** move gold between Morten's purse and the tower's treasury, free, with the orders. The treasury pays purse actions and goal prices; the purse buys at the trader.

sections.title: Morten's month: travel and missions
sections.md:
Travel as in section 1, one hex a day, wandering checks. Then **one mission in the hex he is in, or none.** Strike, Rob and Aid are D&D fights built by encounter; Contact is a check.

| Mission | Where | The fight | On a win |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Strike SITE** | a realm's hex with one of its sites | the site's list at its tier (section 4): seat tier +1, garrison the realm's tier, works tier −1, walls the realm's tier | the realm's goal **−2 marks** (min 0; a goal that waited full is no longer done); standing −1 (seat −2); and marks on the tower's goal where section 10 says so |
| **Rob** | a realm's hex with its works | the works' list at the realm's tier −1 (the same fight as a Strike on them) | **100 × its Force GP** from its treasury (at most what it holds) to the tower's treasury (withdraw it next month); standing −1; the tower's goal +0 |
| **Aid REALM** | the hex its goal is aimed at: a *take*'s hex; the **target's seat** for *raid*, *press* and *break REALM*; the aided realm's own seat for *fortify* (that hex), *raise* and *squeeze* | the obstacle: a goal against another realm, that realm's garrison list at that realm's tier; otherwise the hex's beasts at the aided realm's tier. A goal aimed at the tower (*break*, *raid* or *court the tower*, a *take* of a tower hex) can't be aided | the realm's goal **+2 marks**; standing +1 (to at most +1); and **+2 on the tower's goal** if it is *ally REALM* |
| **Contact REALM** | any of its hexes | no fight: Persuasion (CHA) vs **DC 12 + 3 if the ruler is bad − 2 × standing + 4 while it is squeezed** (a wary bad ruler DC 17, a neutral good one DC 12, a friendly good one DC 10). Standing −2 refuses | standing +1 (to at most +1); at +1 or more after that, a **dissident** is named (needed to topple, section 10); +1 on the tower's goal if it is *ally REALM* |
| **Delve** | the floor under the hex | as in the dungeon game | no domain effect |

A win means every foe dead, fled or surrendered, or the check made. Pass a mission to turn only when it succeeded. **Death** ends the month: the mission fails, he loses the coins and gems he carried, he wakes at the tower; purse actions stand. The trader is at the tower.

At Power (tier 3) the 2s above are 3s: a Strike takes 3 marks off and gives 3, an Aid adds 3 and gives 3. Contact's and Give's +1 stay +1.

sections.title: The tower's goal
sections.md:
The tower keeps **one goal at a time**, declared by the human with the month's orders and kept until done or dropped. Declaring a different goal while one runs drops the old one and **loses its marks** (declaring the same one again changes nothing); Its marks come from Morten's missions and from allies, never from a die. Its clock is set when it is declared and doesn't change after. A full clock fires at the world's turn, and the tower has no goal until the human declares the next.

| Goal | Clock | Needs | Marks from | When the clock is full |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **take HEX** from REALM | 2 + the holder's Force (3–7; +2 if walled) | HEX held by a realm (any realm, anywhere) | a won Strike on any site in HEX +2; an ally +1 a month | the hex is the tower's with its garrison, works and walls (a seat there moves to the loser's deepest hex left); standing with the loser −2; Renown +1. If HEX changes hands first, the goal is dropped at the world's turn and the report says so |
| **ally REALM** | 3 | REALM not an ally | Contact +1; Aid +2; Give 200 GP +1 (once a month); no ally's mark | standing +2; Renown +1. Done at once if REALM courts its way to +2 on its own |
| **topple REALM** | 3 + its Force (4–8) | a **dissident** named there | a Strike on its seat +2; on its garrison, works or walls +1; Give 200 GP to the dissident +1 (once a month); an ally +1 a month | the dissident rules with a random title and a random good tag, full treasury kept, Force kept, standing +2, the realm picks a new goal by its new tag at once, the dissident is cleared; Renown +2 |

At Power the 2s are 3s (the garrison's +1 stays). A Strike on a site of the target realm outside HEX adds nothing to *take HEX*; a Strike adds nothing to *ally REALM*. A realm that courts its way to +2 while the tower's goal is *ally REALM* ends that goal at once: the clock fills and fires that turn.

So the road to the throne is a thing you can watch fill: Contact twice to find the dissident, then Strike the seat while an ally adds a mark a month. And "conquer the world" is literal on the map: take the hexes you want, ally the good rulers, topple the bad ones.

sections.title: Rulers
sections.md: As v2: a name from the people's list, a title, a label and a tag, always shown as **label: verb** ("Reeve Galen (bad: takes people for soldiers)"), everywhere. Rulers change only when the tower **topples** them (section 10): the dissident takes the throne with a random good tag. There is no regime HP and no random collapse; what happens to a realm is on its goal line.

sections.title: Report style
sections.md:
How the GM reports fights and events in chat. At the table (see **The table**) the same voice writes the page's sections and beats, and the dials are the page's own; what follows says how each kind of report reads. It's a set of dials: the human can turn any of them ("fights as outcomes", "domain as log", "more detail on the dice"), and the current setting goes in the GM's notes. Whatever the dials say, the full roll-by-roll log always goes in the GM's notes and the dice are rolled as usual, so the fights can be checked.

**The dials**

| Dial | Default | Other settings |
|---|---|---|
| Fights | **summary** | **log**: the round-by-round Reply format below · **outcome**: one or two lines per fight (foes, result, HP and spells lost, XP and gold) |
| Domain turns | **summary** | **report**: the script's four-part report as it prints |
| Events (travel, shopping, rests, rituals, loot) | **summary** | **log**: one line per event with its rolls |
| Dice in summaries | **key rolls** (nat 20s, nat 1s, fizzles, and the roll that decided the fight) | **none** · **all** |
| Live updates | **every round** | **turning points** (a fizzle, a crit, a kill, a big hit) · **off** (the report only) |

When the human plays Morten turn by turn, a fight is always shown in the **log** format, because the human needs the board to choose Morten's move. The dials matter when the GM (or the AI player) plays several turns or fights in one reply.

**Voice.** The model is the first session: a GM talking the human through the fight, relaxed, with some detail, never a form filled in. In practice:

- **Lead with the headline,** in a full sentence: "Morten cleared the library without taking a single point of damage, and every spell he cast worked. Two natural 20s helped." Then the detail.
- **Say the plan and why,** in Morten's voice when the GM plays him: "Motionless skeletons around a lectern look like a trap, so he never goes near it; the floating hand does." Number the tricks when there are several (Cheese 1, Cheese 2, …).
- **Explain a rule when it matters,** in a short aside: "An unconscious target fails the save automatically, so it's coated."
- **Let the drama of the dice show** in plain words: "Shield just fizzled, so two of them are about to land bites."
- **Group rounds under a short heading** (Round 1 · Initiative: …) with a few lines each, and fold routine rounds together ("R7–R8: Dash to the sleeping worg").
- **End with the stakes and a question:** what he carries and could lose, what's still below, the open choices.
- **Vary it.** Use labels and structure where they help; don't force every fight into the same template.

What makes a report formulaic, and is to be avoided: a fixed set of labels on every fight; every line opening with the same prefix ("R3 · Morten (GM):"); fragments like "Cast (20). Both fail (3, 12)." instead of sentences; a stream of one-liners, one per die call; and bare numbers with no unit.

**Units on every number.** HP, damage, AC, squares and metres always carry their unit or word: "Fire Bolt hits for 8 dmg", "Boar B 13 → 9 HP", "Morten 17/20 HP", "AC 15", "6 sq (9 m)". Never a bare "B 11 · C 6" or "Morten 20 → 17". Dice shown in a roll keep their form (d20 14 +5 = 19 vs AC 15, HIT → 2d6: 3+4 = 7 dmg).

**Live updates.** While the GM plays a fight, it reports as the dice fall instead of playing the whole fight and reporting at the end. The updates go out as chat text between the dice calls, at a natural pace: a line when Morten tries something that matters and why, and a sentence or two when it resolves, with both sides' HP. A quiet round can share a line with the next. When the fight ends, a short wrap-up follows: the headline and the result, not a replay of rounds the human has just watched.

Round 2 · Thunderwave on the three snakes lined up beside him. The cast holds (16), two of them fail their saves, and 11 thunder dmg kills all three. Morten is on 11/20 HP.

**Monsters show their CR.** Every time a monster is named in a heading, a stat line or a fight report, give its CR next to it, with the fight's difficulty and XP: "3 Venomous Snakes (CR 1/8 each) · Moderate, 75 XP". A mixed group gives each kind's CR.

**Fights: summary.** When fights aren't watched live (live updates off, or a fight reported afterwards), one block per fight: a heading with the room or place, the foes and their CR, the difficulty and XP, and a few words of verdict; then the story in a few bullets, using labels such as Prep, Scouting, Cheese, The dice, How it ended and Result only where they have something to say. Keep the numbers that matter (HP, the damage that nearly killed him, XP, gold) and leave the rest to the transcript.

**Room 3.1 · 3 Boars (CR 1/4 each) · Low, 150 XP · cleared, but barely**
- **Cheese:** Web across the approach to the door. Two boars got stuck in round 1, and the third waded through.
- **The dice:** 5 spells fizzled, each lost for the day: Scorching Ray (the Heroic Inspiration reroll still landed 1 short), Magic Missile, Shocking Grasp, Shield and Misty Step.
- **How it ended:** Sleep dropped one boar, but a natural 1 on concentration woke it. He finished the last two with a dagger and Ray of Frost while backing up the stair.
- **Result:** cleared on **1 HP**, potion used. XP 1,150 → 1,300. +15 GP.

**Domain turns: summary.** Keep the four parts (The plan, What happened, The tower now, Next month), but write What happened as one or two plain sentences per event: who (*label: verb*), what they did, what goal it served, how it came out, and what it means for the tower ("The Gnomes march Thugs and Knights into C4 to rob the Tieflings; that's two hexes from the tower, but they aren't after us"). Give an attack's roll in brief only when it decided something. Next month says the threats and chances in words, then the open choices.

**Events: summary.** A few bullets per day or stop: travel and wandering checks (only an encounter gets more than a clause), shopping with the coins left, rests with what came back, loot. Fold routine steps into one line.

**After a run of several fights** (a floor, a month), end with a short wrap-up: where Morten stands (HP, XP, level, gold, what's lost), what worked and what didn't, any rulings made along the way, and what's next.
